default_page_title: OSPF visualization and analysis offline for network engineers
og_default_title: OSPF/IS-IS topology visualization and analysis offline for network engineers
page_none_loaded: 0 of {total} loaded - load more to search the rest
facet_truncated: Only the first {count} values are listed - narrow the search
event_open: Open the graph at this time
event_still_down: still down at the end of the period
events_lanes_note: Adjacency bar runs from down to up (how long the link was down), as on the current timeline; metrics and networks are timestamps.
events_routers_note: A lane is the router that detected the event (event_detected_by); colour is the category.
period_outside: The period is outside the graph's history.
routers_shown: Routers {from}-{to} of {total}, by number of events
zoom_hint: drag over a span to zoom in
delete_watcher_graph_note: If a watcher feeds it, that watcher stays registered and keeps sending, so a new graph appears with its next data. To stop it, delete the watcher on Monitoring.
history_enterprise_note: Event history and monitoring are available in Topolograph Enterprise.
agent_open: Ask the agent about the network
agent_mon_hint: The agent explains the events: what happened and how it changed paths
agent_explain_hint: Ask the agent about this event
agent_off_p1: This Topolograph install has no agent address set, so questions are not sent. Below are examples of what the agent answers.
agent_off_connect: The agent is connected with the {variable} variable in the Topolograph .env file; after the service restarts, the window starts answering.
agent_placeholder_landing: A question about the demo network: paths, failures, events, LSP
